voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: Between 1986 and 1991, ten women were murdered in rural South Korea.
The case went cold — and stayed cold for more than thirty years.
One innocent man served twenty years for one of the murders — convicted on a coerced confession.
In 2019, DNA identified the real killer. He confessed to fourteen murders.
The law's own statute of limitations meant he could never be charged for any of them.
The full story is on the channel.
